claim: Explicit prosody reference frame is task-dependent
boundary: Relative pitch improves categorical emotion but strongly hurts gender/trait decoding across ESD, MEAD, RAVDESS.

claim: Categorical emotion reference preference is class- and attribute-dependent
boundary: Per-emotion and per-attribute effects change sign; no universal Relative winner.

claim: WavLM retains both absolute and relative reference information
boundary: Absolute, relative, and implied baseline pitch are highly decodable; relative information weakens in later layers.

claim: Raw VAD preference depends on target between-speaker structure
boundary: Controlled lambda intervention yields significantly negative Relative-minus-Absolute slopes for Arousal/Dominance in MSP and IEMOCAP.
Linear and quadratic Ridge preserve negative Arousal/Dominance slopes in both corpora.
Pitch, loudness, and rate all show coupling somewhere; magnitude differs strongly by corpus/attribute.

claim: Correct speaker-center identity causes raw-VAD Hybrid utility
boundary: Permuting speaker centers destroys large MSP raw Arousal/Dominance gains while residual targets are nearly unchanged.

claim: Unlabeled enrollment can recover useful speaker reference
boundary: K-shot Hybrid is useful; K about 20 is near practical saturation in MSP. IEMOCAP K-shot slope recovery is noisier/non-monotonic.

claim: IEMOCAP external replication survives without ambiguous loudness
boundary: Pitch+rate slopes remain significantly negative for Arousal/Dominance under linear and quadratic Ridge.
